To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed multilevel LV RD design is more efficient than conventional CRD designs and that the proposed method can provide a more accurate estimate of LATE than the conventional CRD design when there is a large ME in the RV.

(a) the proposed multilevel LV CRD model is more accurate than the conventional CRD in the recovery of the LATE; (b) the conventional CRD is biased when there is a large ME in the RV and/or the cluster size is small; and (c) the proposed model is computationally feasible and provides a more accurate estimation of the LATE than the conventional CRRD model
the proposed latent variable RD model outperforms conventional CRD models in the estimation of treatment effects when the running variable is measured with error.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a multilevel LV model for the RD design.
improving the validity of RD design in the presence of ME in RV and sampling design.
the estimation of the LATE under a hierarchical design with a noisy running variable that is a noisy measure of a latent construct.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model outperformed the conventional model across all conditions, with the exception of one condition where the two models performed comparably.

the proposed multilevel LV model with the MH RM algorithm is a viable alternative to the conventional CRD design when the data are hierarchical and the running variable is a latent construct measured with error.
the proposed multilevel LV model is superior to the conventional CRD approach in terms of statistical efficiency and generalization of the estimated causal effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a multivariate latent regression discontinuity design with a cluster level treatment assignment.
the multilevel latent CRD design with the MH-RM algorithm can be a valuable alternative for estimating the LATE in educational or clinical research.
our model provides more accurate estimates of the treatment effect than the conventional model, especially in situations where the measurement model has a complex structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed model is a more appropriate approach to estimate LATEs when the running variables are latent constructs.
researchers should not rely on the conventional RD model to make inferences about treatment effects.
researchers can benefit from using the multilevel latent CRD design when the running variable is a noisy measure of a latent construct and data are hierarchically structured.
